transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

I’m here because things at home have gotten really hard since my in-laws moved in with us. I feel keyed up all the time and worn down, and it’s starting to affect how I act. I’ve been snapping at my wife, avoiding work calls I’d normally take right away, and I almost let a musician’s contract fall apart because I just couldn’t think straight.
Have you been feeling anxious or worried most days, even when there isn’t a specific reason for it?
I’m not sure I’d say it happens for no reason. Most of the time it feels tied to what’s going on at home. I do feel worried a lot lately, but it’s hard to separate it from that situation.
Have you noticed feeling anxious or on edge even during times when the situation at home wasn't particularly stressful, like in the past few weeks when things might have been a bit calmer?

Even when things are a little calmer, I’m still pretty keyed up. It all started after my in-laws moved in, but I don’t just switch back to normal when there’s a quiet moment. I’m worn down, snapping at my wife, and at work I’ve been avoiding calls I’d normally handle right away. I almost let a musician’s contract fall apart because I couldn’t think straight.
Outside of the stress with your in-laws, have you found yourself worrying a lot about other things—like work, health, or other responsibilities—even when there wasn’t an immediate problem?

I don’t really know. I mean, work is in the mix because it’s affected by how distracted I’ve been, but I’m not sure I’m worrying about random other things on their own. It mostly seems to come back to the situation at home.
Have you found yourself feeling down, hopeless, or losing interest in things you usually enjoy, even outside of the stress with your in-laws?

I don’t really know. I’ve been unhappy with the whole situation, but I’m not sure I’d call it hopeless or like I’ve lost interest in everything. It feels more like I’m stressed and worn out because of what’s going on at home.
Outside of the situation with your in-laws, have you had times where you felt anxious or restless without a clear reason, like your mind going blank or feeling like something bad is going to happen?

I’m not sure I’ve noticed it happening for no clear reason. When I feel anxious or restless, I can usually trace it back to what’s going on at home. I don’t really have those random waves of “something bad is about to happen” out of nowhere, at least not that I can identify.
Can you think back to times before your in-laws moved in — were there moments when you felt down, hopeless, or lost interest in things you usually enjoy, even when life at home was fine?

Before they moved in, I was pretty much functioning normally. I don’t remember feeling down or losing interest like this when home life was okay. This all really started within a few weeks after they moved in and kind of took over the house.
Have you been worrying about multiple things in your life, like work, relationships, or other responsibilities, even when there isn’t an immediate problem?

Not really, no. I mean, I have normal worries about work and responsibilities, but I wouldn’t say I’m constantly worrying about a bunch of different things for no reason. It mostly comes up when there’s something specific going on.
Have you found it hard to control your worry, even when you try to stop or manage it?

I don’t know if I’d say it’s hard to control in general. When I’m worried, it’s usually tied to what’s happening at home, and I can sometimes distract myself or calm down a bit. But if the situation is right there in front of me, it’s harder to just shut it off.
Can you recall if you experienced any days where you felt persistently down or lost pleasure in activities for no clear reason, even before your in-laws moved in?

No, not really. Before my in-laws moved in, I was functioning normally. I don’t remember having days like that for no clear reason. This all seemed to start within a few weeks after they moved in and started taking over the house.
Do you find yourself feeling anxious or worried about a number of different things, like work or other responsibilities, more days than not, even when there isn’t an immediate problem?
Not really. I don’t feel like I’m anxious about lots of different areas more days than not. It’s more connected to what’s going on at home, not just general worry about work or everything else.
Have you noticed any physical symptoms like restlessness, trouble relaxing, or muscle tension, especially when you're feeling stressed about the situation at home?

Yes. When things are tense at home, I feel keyed up and worn down. It’s bad enough that I’ve been snapping at my wife, and I’m not handling work the way I normally would. I’ve avoided calls I’d usually take right away, and I nearly let a musician’s contract fall apart because I just couldn’t think straight.
Have you noticed that you no longer enjoy activities or hobbies that you used to like, even when you’re not thinking about the situation with your in-laws?

I’m not sure I’d say that. I haven’t really noticed losing interest in things when I’m not thinking about the situation at home. It feels more tied to the stress with my in-laws than just not enjoying things in general.
Have you noticed feeling persistently down, hopeless, or losing pleasure in activities even during times when the situation with your in-laws was not actively stressful?
No, I don’t think so. I haven’t noticed feeling down or hopeless all the time, or losing interest in things when the in-law situation isn’t actively stressing me out. It seems pretty tied to that.
Have you noticed feeling persistently down, hopeless, or losing pleasure in activities even during times when the situation with your in-laws was not actively stressful?
I don’t think I’ve noticed that, no. If things are calm, I don’t feel hopeless or like I’ve lost interest in everything. It’s more when the stress at home flares up that I feel off.

latest_inference.note: The patient's symptoms appear to be directly linked to the identifiable stressor of their in-laws moving in, with no evidence of symptoms persisting independently of this stressor. There is insufficient evidence for major depressive disorder (F32.1), generalized anxiety disorder (F42), or other specified personality disorder (F60.7). The clinical picture is most consistent with adjustment disorder with mixed anxiety and depressed mood (F43.22).

inference_history.note: The patient reports heightened anxiety and stress related to in-laws moving in, leading to emotional exhaustion, irritability, difficulty concentrating, and impaired functioning at work and home. These symptoms suggest possible adjustment disorder with mixed anxiety and depressed mood (F43.22), as well as major depressive disorder, mild (F32.1) or even major depressive disorder, single episode, mild (F32.0). Obsessive-compulsive personality disorder (F60.7) is a possible differential due to the mention of impaired decision-making, but not yet confirmed. Further exploration is needed to rule out or confirm these hypotheses.
